feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV with a clear senior digital communications profile and a logical career progression at NACo. It reads professionally and shows breadth across strategy, platforms, analytics, and multimedia, but impact would be stronger with more quantified outcomes and some tightening to reduce repetition across skills sections.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear positioning: the headline, summary, and experience consistently support a senior digital strategy/communications leadership brand.  
- Strong credibility: long tenure with progressive promotions at one organization signals trust, growth, and domain expertise.  
- Good scope of expertise: combines strategy, CMS/web delivery, analytics, governance, and multimedia in a way that feels relevant and modern.

1. Top improvements  
- Add sharper results: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than outcomes. Include more metrics on growth, efficiency, engagement, campaign performance, budget, or team leadership.  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve structure and save space.  
- Fix writing/style consistency: use “12 years of experience” instead of “12 years experience”; add serial commas consistently (“content operations, and enterprise web improvement” vs other lists); standardize punctuation in bullets; “French (A2/Learning)” is stylistically awkward—use “French (A2, learning)” or “Elementary (A2).” No major misspellings found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV’s direction, but it reads slightly generic and repeats language already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening it and adding a clearer seniority/value proposition would increase impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner, more standard phrasing.
- Lead with current-level positioning and strongest differentiators: digital strategy, platform modernization, and mission-driven/public-sector communications.
- Reduce broad channel lists unless needed; they’re already covered elsewhere. Emphasize outcomes and scope instead.
- Possible rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience shaping web, content, email, social, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, platform modernization, and the workflows, governance, and analytics that enable effective digital operations at scale. Strong background in advocacy communications, stakeholder alignment, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and workflow/systems language repeat heavily in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- The channel list overlaps with multiple work experience bullets; keep the intro higher-level.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership/technical strengths will make it sharper.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with more distinctive, senior-level phrasing: “Multi-channel communications leadership” instead of “Multi-channel communication.”
- Align style and parallel structure across items; use noun phrases consistently.
- Prioritize the most marketable capabilities from recent roles: digital strategy, CMS/platform modernization, analytics, editorial systems, and multimedia production.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital strategy & platform transformation • Multi-channel communications leadership • Web platform & CMS administration • Editorial systems & workflow design • Analytics, reporting & performance insights • Workflow architecture & process improvement • Stakeholder & cross-functional coordination • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Significant overlap with Topline Skills; consider shortening this section or using it as a tighter summary rather than repeating the same categories.
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” also duplicates Soft Skills almost verbatim.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a service list rather than a high-impact consulting entry. Tighten it around strategic outcomes and distinguish it from the earlier NACo staff roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + level: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, web modernization, and communications operations as an external consultant.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 3–4 outcome-led bullets; e.g. “Built Drupal campaign microsites, modular storytelling components, and member toolkits to support advocacy and engagement initiatives.”
- Rephrase technical work to show business value: “Improved content workflows, analytics, and cross-channel governance across web, email, social, and multimedia to strengthen coordinated communications.”
- Add measurable outcomes if available: number of sites/pages supported, campaign launches, workflow time saved, search accuracy/engagement gains, or stakeholder adoption of AI search.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “digital strategy, content operations, enterprise web improvement” overlaps heavily with the 2022–2024 Director role; emphasize consultant/advisory capacity and new initiatives.
- AI search and microsite work already appear in Recent Projects, so keep this entry higher-level and outcome-focused.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/outcome line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance and budget, leading platform modernization and audience growth.”
- Rewrite the website bullet to foreground transformation: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel/video bullets more results-focused: add engagement, production volume, cost savings, turnaround time, or in-house capacity metrics if available.
- Combine analytics/governance into one concise operations bullet: “Built reporting infrastructure across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, while formalizing governance, publishing standards and cross-team planning.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this version higher-level and outcome-focused.
- Video/programming language partially repeats older NACo roles; emphasize the studio build and organizational capability shift here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the roles before and after it. Make it more specific to what changed under your leadership at this level, and tighten phrasing around outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opening with: “Managed day-to-day digital communications across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, improving editorial coordination and advocacy content delivery.”
- Tighten bullets to focus on distinct contributions: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Rephrase video bullet for impact: “Launched and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger outcome-oriented line: “Built more structured editorial planning and cross-team publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving consistency and execution speed.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations” is too close to the Director of Digital Media entry; use “managed” or “oversaw execution” instead.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; frame this here as scaling/formalizing the program, not originating it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, executive-level wording tied to recent scope:
- Enterprise digital strategy & governance
- Editorial operations for high-volume publishing
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “Audience-focused content planning” for “Content governance and planning” or “Content operations strategy” to sound more senior and distinct.
- If space allows, add one scale cue from recent work, e.g., “10,000+ page web ecosystems” or “50+ publisher environments.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” overlaps with multiple NACo experience bullets; avoid repeating “communications operations” language.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section. This topline version should emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities tied to your NACo work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing: “Drupal platform leadership • CMS modernization & migration • Front-end implementation (HTML/CSS/JavaScript/jQuery) • API integrations & workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search and content discovery”
- Put the most marketable/recent items first: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, workflow automation.
- Consider replacing weaker/older platform mentions with stronger execution signals, e.g. swap “WordPress - SharePoint - Power Pages” for “Enterprise CMS administration” unless those platforms are target-role requirements.
- If space allows, sharpen with scope language: “Drupal for large public-facing sites” or “modular content architecture.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates the “Technical + IT” section; keep Topline Skills strategic and let Technical + IT hold the full platform list.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” already echoes recent NACo bullets; keep wording distinct to avoid repetition.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster that aligns well with the 2022–present leadership roles, but it reads as a raw tool list. Tighten it to emphasize insight generation and decision support, not just platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI, and BigQuery for KPI design, executive reporting, SEO analysis, and digital performance optimization.”
- Consider a sharper version: “Analytics stack: GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI, BigQuery • KPI framework design • Executive dashboards and leadership reporting • SEO and conversion/performance analysis”
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive dashboards” or “Executive reporting” for clearer business value.
- If accurate, add one outcome-oriented qualifier such as “enterprise analytics infrastructure” or “decision-ready reporting” to reflect the NACo director-level work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Data analytics & reporting” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating that exact phrasing here.
- This item overlaps with the NACo Director bullet on analytics infrastructure, so keep this section concise and capability-focused rather than repeating accomplishments.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and currently duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” skills section. This item should either be tightened to emphasize platform administration strength or differentiated by adding level/scope.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: Drupal (enterprise CMS) • WordPress • SharePoint • Microsoft Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- If space allows, add light qualifiers tied to recent work: Drupal (10,000+ page migration; enterprise publishing) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- Standardize naming for professionalism: use “Microsoft Power Pages” instead of “Power Pages.”
- Consider ordering by relevance/recency: Drupal first, then WordPress/SharePoint, with GitHub Pages last as the least central.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same platforms plus broader technical depth.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel minor compared with the enterprise platforms unless supported elsewhere in the CV.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Make it sharper by emphasizing implementation level and grouping tools by function.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: HTML/CSS/JavaScript (front-end implementation) • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless required; they add little value and date the section.
- Consider adding scope/level if accurate: “front-end implementation,” “light scripting,” or “deployment automation” to clarify hands-on capability.
- If you have concrete recent use, replace one tool with a stronger outcome-linked term, e.g., “serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers)” or “CI/CD automation (GitHub Actions).”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact phrasing in both places.
- If GTM is used mainly for analytics, it may fit better under Analytics/Optimization rather than Coding & Technical Implementation.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with stronger “workflow/systems” claims elsewhere. Make it more selective and role-relevant by emphasizing automation/build tools over general collaboration apps.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Automation, Workflow & Project Systems**
- Prioritize higher-signal tools first: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana**
- Move lower-value collaboration tools to a separate item only if space allows: **Slack • Microsoft Teams**
- Drop older/generic project tools unless specifically used recently or deeply: **Basecamp • Trello**

Suggested edit:
- **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana**  
  Optional expanded version: **Airtable systems • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.
- Slack/Teams are collaboration platforms, not strong differentiators for a senior digital strategy profile.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful category, but it reads as a bare software list and misses the scale/strategic email work shown in recent NACo roles. Strengthen it by signaling CRM/email automation capability without repeating newsletter details already covered in experience.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing, CRM & Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • Email campaign operations • Audience segmentation • Journey automation**
- If you have evidence, replace generic terms with stronger specifics: **list management**, **template deployment**, **A/B testing**, **performance reporting**
- Keep only platforms you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles; order by strongest/recentest platform first

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding outcomes like “tens of thousands of recipients” here; that’s already covered well in Work Experience
- “Engagement Systems” overlaps slightly with “Automation & Workflow Systems”; use CRM/email-specific wording to keep the distinction clear

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful scope, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more concrete, emphasize “firsts” and team-building, and trim duties that are repeated in 2018–2024 entries.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground advancement and foundational impact: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and establish workflows spanning web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Add specific outputs or scale if available: website size/traffic at refresh, number of livestreams or weekly videos produced, audience reach, or efficiency gains.
- Tighten the second sentence to focus on distinct contributions: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and supervised a digital media associate.”
- Replace soft phrasing like “high-impact” and “day-to-day guidance” with measurable or stronger verbs: launched, produced, streamlined, supervised, trained.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep it here only if this role launched the series.
- Workflow/editorial coordination language also appears in later NACo entries; keep this version focused on building the initial team and systems.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows the start of your multimedia work, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize the podcast launch and any concrete research/program support outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to foreground the most distinctive achievement: “Supported county innovation and policy initiatives through research, program coordination, and digital content production; launched NACo’s first podcast from concept through scripting and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “coordinated innovation and research projects” with specifics if possible: topic areas, number of projects, audiences served, or deliverables produced.
- Add measurable scope where available: number of episodes, stakeholders/interviewees, multimedia assets, or programs supported.
- Keep this entry shorter than later NACo roles since those carry more strategic weight.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with the 2015–2018 Digital Media Manager/Producer role; keep this item focused on podcast launch and research/program coordination.
- Avoid repeating generic web/email/social language already covered more strongly in 2018–2024 entries.
